[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Pre-trained Language Models (BERT, GPT, T5)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) have fundamentally transformed Natural Language Processing (NLP). By leveraging massive unannotated corpora, these models learn rich semantic and syntactic representations that can be fine-tuned for downstream tasks with minimal task-specific data. This tutorial explores the architectural differences, training objectives, and practical implementation of three prominent PLM paradigms: BERT (Encoder-only), GPT (Decoder-only), and T5 (Encoder-Decoder)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Architectural Paradigms"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers): Utilizes only the Transformer encoder. It processes context from both left and right simultaneously, making it ideal for understanding tasks like sentiment analysis, named entity recognition, and question answering."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer): Utilizes only the Transformer decoder with causal masked self-attention. Tokens can only attend to preceding tokens, making it optimal for autoregressive generation tasks like text completion and dialogue systems."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer): Employs the full encoder-decoder architecture. T5 re-frames all NLP problems into a unified text-to-text format, taking text as input and generating new text as output, seamlessly handling translation, summarization, and classification."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Pre-training Objectives"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Each model is defined by how it is pre-trained. BERT uses Masked Language Modeling (MLM), where 15 percent of input tokens are replaced with a special [MASK] token, and the model must predict the original tokens. GPT uses Causal Language Modeling (CLM), predicting the next token given all previous tokens. T5 uses a span-corruption objective, masking random contiguous spans of tokens and requiring the model to generate the missing spans."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Practical Implementation with Hugging Face Transformers"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following Python code snippet demonstrates how to load tokenizers and models for BERT, GPT-2, and T5 using the Hugging Face transformers library."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM

# 1. BERT (Masked Language Modeling)
bert_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
bert_model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')

# 2. GPT (Causal Language Generation)
gpt_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('gpt2')
gpt_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('gpt2')

# 3. T5 (Text-to-Text Generation)
t5_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('t5-small')
t5_model = AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained('t5-small')

print('Successfully loaded BERT, GPT, and T5 architectures.')"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Tokenization and Forward Pass Example"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let us examine how to process inputs for T5, treating a text classification task as a text-to-text problem."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"input_text = "sst2 sentence: This movie is absolutely fantastic!"
inputs = t5_tokenizer(input_text, return_tensors="pt")

# Generate output using the T5 model
outputs = t5_model.generate(**inputs, max_length=10)
decoded_output = t5_tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

print(f"Model Prediction: {decoded_output}")"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right pre-trained language model depends heavily on your specific application. Use BERT and its variants for discriminative tasks requiring deep bidirectional context, GPT for generative tasks and few-shot prompting, and T5 when you require a flexible, unified framework for diverse sequence-to-sequence transformations."}]
